# cuteafd-eval

> Results-first public ledger: two inference engines by tpurtell (CuteAFD and tpurtell's vLLM fork) serving GLM-5.3-Flash EXL3
> quantizations on one machine (2x NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Max-Q). Maintained by Michael M (UrbanAstroLA).

Every page is generated from the files in the repository; numbers are never typed into pages. Start with the
machine-readable files below rather than scraping HTML.

## Machine-readable entry points
- https://urbanastrola.github.io/cuteafd-eval/findings.json: the Thinking length investigation's claims, one entry per claim, with status, value,
  95% interval, a JSON pointer into the source file, and the per-reply data and script that recompute it.
- https://github.com/UrbanAstroLA/cuteafd-eval/tree/main/results: one folder per run. In each: RUN.json (id, kind, title, protocol, engine,
  checkpoints), SUMMARY.json (every number its page shows), MANIFEST.json (sha256 of every file), README.md.
- results/*/analysis/samples.csv: one row per reply (arm, prompt, seed, finish, reasoning tokens, decode speed, tests).
- https://github.com/UrbanAstroLA/cuteafd-eval/blob/main/protocol/README.md: the frozen protocol; protocol/HASHES.json binds published files to it.

## How to read the results
- Run kinds: measurement (protocol frozen before the first request), exploratory (evidence, not a frozen comparison),
  check. A finding's status says which; post hoc numbers are labelled post hoc.
- Intervals are 95% bootstrap intervals over the unit named (prompts, questions, windows); "detected" means the interval
  excludes the null (1 for ratios, 0 for differences). Bootstrap seeds differ per run: see each run's protocol, or
  recompute.bootstrap in findings.json.
- "Finished" = finish_reason stop and not capped. Medians are over finished replies. findings.json has a definitions block
  with every estimator used.
- findings.json pointers are RFC 6901: unescape ~1 to / and ~0 to ~ after splitting (some keys contain a slash).
- Thinking-length ratios put K4-Core-K6, or the part under test, first: above 1 = it thought longer. Each finding states
  its own direction.
- Numbers from different model families or tokenizers are not comparable; NLL is per tokenizer.
- "BF16 core" means different things on the two engines: BF16 matrices on the vLLM fork, BF16 converted to FP8 at load on
  CuteAFD v4.0.0. The vLLM fork runs with a local loader modification, not a tpurtell release; derived checkpoints are
  local builds, not producer releases.

## Validate
- `python3 tools/verify.py` checks every manifest hash, every site link and anchor, every findings.json pointer, and
  recomputes the code-study ratios and test counts from the per-reply tables.
- Each run folder's code/ and analysis/ hold the scripts that produced its numbers; repro/REPRODUCE.md covers re-running.

## Status vocabulary in findings.json
- measurement: frozen rule: protocol and decision rule frozen (hashes in the run's protocol/FROZEN.json) before the first request
- measurement: post hoc: computed from frozen-run data after the run; not part of any decision rule
- measurement: descriptive: counted from frozen-run data; not part of any decision rule
- exploratory: run kind exploratory: useful evidence, not a frozen comparison
- source reading: read in source code and logs, no measurement
- in progress: running; no result published

## Thinking length findings (summary)
- TL-code-vllm-core [measurement: frozen rule]: On the vLLM fork, does K4-Core-K6's 6-bit core change how long code replies think, against the original BF16 core? No: 1.00x [0.96, 1.04], not detected.
- TL-code-cuteafd-core [measurement: frozen rule]: On CuteAFD v4.0.0, does the native 6-bit core change how long code replies think, against the BF16 core converted to FP8 at load? Yes: 1.26x [1.24, 1.29], detected, every prompt above 1. See TL-code-engines and TL-code-fp8-arm for which arm differs and TL-fp8-ablation for which FP8 setting carries it.
- TL-code-engines [measurement: frozen rule]: Do the two engines agree on the core's effect on code thinking length? No: vLLM ratio / CuteAFD ratio = 0.79 [0.75, 0.83] (exp of the vLLM log ratio minus the CuteAFD log ratio, paired by prompt). By the reading stated before the run, the CuteAFD gap goes with how CuteAFD serves the core, not with the weight values.
- TL-code-fp8-arm [measurement: post hoc]: Which of the four code configurations thinks differently? CuteAFD's BF16-core configuration (core, KDA projections, vocabulary head and prefill activations in FP8): 0.82x the vLLM BF16 core on the 12 new prompts (0.78x over all 16), shorter on every prompt; the other three sit within about 4% of each other.
- TL-code-tests [measurement: descriptive]: Does the length difference change the result on code? No measurable change in replies passing all hidden tests on either engine.
- TL-fp8-path [source reading]: What differs between CuteAFD's two core formats besides the core's weights? With a BF16 core, CuteAFD v4.0.0's launcher also puts the KDA projections (including three gate projections outside the core) and the vocabulary head in FP8, and prefill runs the MLA and MLP projections with FP8 activations; with the native 6-bit core these stay on the 6-bit kernels or in BF16. On a two-GPU head split the FP8 KDA path also comes with KDA output sharding, which v4 accepts only with FP8 KDA and clears for the native core.
- TL-fp8-ablation [measurement: frozen rule]: Which part of CuteAFD's FP8 path goes with the shorter code reasoning of the BF16-core checkpoint (local derived checkpoint, not a producer release)? The KDA launch setting: switching the KDA projections from FP8 to BF16 (on this two-GPU layout that also turns off KDA output sharding, which v4 runs only with FP8 KDA) gives 1.31x [1.24, 1.38], detected, every prompt above 1; then the vocabulary head 1.02x [0.97, 1.07] and prefill activations 0.99x [0.97, 1.02], not detected. With the KDA setting off the gap to the native 6-bit core closes (C-K6 / F-kda 0.96x [0.92, 1.01]); KDA's share of the gap 1.16 [0.95, 1.37] (above 1 = the point estimate passes the native core; the interval includes 1, consistent with the whole gap). Settings were switched off cumulatively.
- TL-experts [measurement: frozen rule]: Do the routed experts change thinking length? No measurable contribution: 0.99x [0.93, 1.05].
- TL-stop-cuteafd [exploratory]: On CuteAFD, does the core change when the model decides to stop on fixed science-question reasoning traces? No: -0.0144 [-0.0497, +0.0187] on the new questions; no effect on the earlier 11 either.
- TL-stop-vllm [exploratory]: On the vLLM fork, does the core change when the model decides to stop on fixed science-question reasoning traces? No: -0.0109 [-0.0315, +0.0046] on the new questions.
- TL-qbo [exploratory]: Do q_b and the output projections in BF16 move the stop decision? Not in general: +0.0118 on the 11 questions they were found on, -0.0032 [-0.0161, +0.0064] on 30 new questions, not replicated.
- TL-identity [measurement: frozen rule]: Do two launches of the same model agree? CuteAFD: bit-identical on every scored row, also two days later. vLLM fork: no; the launch difference is as large as the core's.

## Pages

## Runs (results/<id>/RUN.json)
- 2026-10-26-cuteafd-setup-checks (check): Core-FP8 expert bytes and FP8 projections checked against K3.25-v1; CuteAFD source audit
- 2026-10-26-cuteafd-vs-vllm (measurement): CuteAFD v3.0.1 vs tpurtell's vLLM fork v0.9.2: precision, throughput, long output
- 2026-10-26-e1-router-route (exploratory): CuteAFD router logits across its 160/161-row route switch (one GPU, one kernel)
- 2026-10-27-k4-vllm-cuteafd (measurement): K4 (brandonmusic GLM-5.3-Flash-tr3-4bpw) on tpurtell's vLLM fork v0.9.2 and CuteAFD v3.0.1: precision, throughput, long output
- 2026-10-27-long-context-pilot (exploratory): Needle retrieval at 256K, 512K and 1M tokens, both engines, K3.25 (one request per prompt and engine)
- 2026-10-27-vllm-startup-cache (measurement): vLLM v0.9.2 startup time with and without persisted JIT caches, and CuteAFD's for comparison
- 2026-10-30-cuteafd-v4 (measurement): CuteAFD v4.0.0 against tpurtell's vLLM fork v0.9.2 on K3.25 and K4, and K4-Core-K6 on CuteAFD v4.0.0
- 2026-11-02-thinking-length (measurement): Thinking length and the 6-bit core of K4-Core-K6: BF16 core-tensor swaps on fixed traces (G2) and in free generation (G4), with loop checks
- 2026-11-02-tool-calling (measurement): Multi-turn tool calling (tool-eval-bench, 88 scenarios): CuteAFD v4.0.0 and the vLLM fork v0.9.2 on K3.25 and K4, CuteAFD on K4-Core-K6
- 2026-11-03-cuteafd-core-swap (measurement): CuteAFD core swap: K4-Core-K6's 6-bit core against its BF16 core (same experts) and against K4, in free generation and on fixed traces
- 2026-11-05-attn-position (exploratory): Does the core's effect grow with position? Position analysis of the fixed-trace dumps, and the vLLM fork with q_b and the output projections in BF16 together
- 2026-11-05-code-thinking (measurement): Code thinking length on CuteAFD: K4-Core-K6's 6-bit core against its BF16 core, 16 code prompts x 4 seeds
- 2026-11-06-cuteafd-fp8-ablation (measurement): Which part of CuteAFD's FP8 path shortens code reasoning: KDA FP8, FP8 head and FP8 prefill switched off cumulatively
- 2026-11-06-new-questions (exploratory): New questions: the q_b + output-projection stop-decision shift and the core, on 30 questions not used before
- 2026-11-06-vllm-code-thinking (measurement): Code thinking length on the vLLM fork: K4-Core-K6's 6-bit core against its BF16 core, 16 code prompts x 4 seeds

## Not published
Model output text (replies, reasoning), benchmark question text, and raw dumps.
